sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports chart pieces
sections.what: Brings in the chart types and the card and store pieces the charts need.
sections.why: Likely reason: each chart type must be imported before it can be drawn. Reason for choosing these exact types not stated.
sections.watch_out: The pie chart pieces are imported, but no pie chart is drawn anywhere in this file.

sections.name: ProductivityChartsProps
sections.title: Accepts the timeframe value
sections.what: Declares that the component receives weekly, monthly or yearly, but the rest of the file never reads it.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Changing the timeframe will not change any chart in this file.

sections.name: ProductivityCharts (part 1)
sections.title: Builds data for the four charts
sections.what: Prepares the numbers for each chart: a score line, focus hours with estimated coding and study shares, completed versus total counts, habit success for six life areas, and time totals by category.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the drawing code simple by doing the arithmetic first.
sections.watch_out: The coding and study hours are fixed shares of total focus time, so they are estimates rather than tracked values.

sections.name: ProductivityCharts (part 2)
sections.title: Pie data and first two charts
sections.what: Creates pie slices from focus time by category, with a no-data slice if nothing is logged. Draws the score trajectory line chart and the focus area chart.
sections.why: Likely reason: the pie data was prepared for a time-allocation view, but no pie is drawn. Reason not stated.
sections.watch_out: The pie data is built but never displayed, so changes to it will not appear on screen.

sections.name: ProductivityCharts (part 3)
sections.title: Bar and radar charts
sections.what: Draws a bar chart comparing completed and total counts, and a radar chart of habit success across six life areas on a 0 to 100 scale.
sections.why: Likely reason: compares progress visually across categories.
sections.watch_out: The radar only includes habits whose category matches one of six exact names, so habits in other categories are left out.

summary: A group of four charts showing score trend, focus time, task completion and balance across life areas.
purpose: Gives visual summaries of the user's productivity data.
why: Likely reason: charts show trends more easily than numbers. The code does not explain the choice of these four charts.
how: Reads the profile, tasks, habits, assignments, projects and focus sessions from the store. Builds a small data set for each chart: a two-point score line, a focus area split, completed versus total counts, and average habit success for six life areas. Also works out time totals by category. Draws the line, area, bar and radar charts in a grid. Pie data is calculated but not drawn.
inputs: Store data from the profile, tasks, habits, assignments, projects and focus sessions. A timeframe value is received but not used.
outputs: Four charts on screen. No data is saved.
risks: The line chart has only two points, a zero starting point and the current score, so it does not show a real trend. The area chart's coding and study figures are fixed shares of focus time, not measured values. Pie data is built but never shown. Habits counted as completed today are actually habits with success above 50 percent.
debug: If a chart is empty, check that the category names in focus sessions and habits match the names the code looks for. If values look odd, check the calculations above the drawing code. If the timeframe seems ignored, that is expected because the value is unused.
